answer.prompt: Image 1 is the room to edit: a bright, empty living room seen from its near end, looking toward a black-framed balcony sliding door. Images 2–9 are each one product to add, by number. Placement: Image 2, the light grey sofa, stands against the long left wall, centered between the two left-wall outlets and the far wall, facing right into the room, about a third of the image width. Image 3, the rug, lies on the floor in front of the sofa, its long side parallel to the left wall, reaching toward the right wall. Image 4, the coffee table, stands on the rug's center, in front of the sofa, about a tenth of the image width. Image 5, the TV stand, stands against the right wall, facing the sofa, partly cut by the right edge of the frame. Image 6, the arc lamp, stands in the far-left corner, between the sofa's far end and the far wall, its arc reaching over the sofa. Image 8, the palm, stands just in front of the far wall, left of the balcony door below the light switch. Image 9, the curtains, hang from a rod above the balcony door, below the AC, drawn to the sides. Image 7, the two cushions, sit on the sofa. Keep the floor near the camera clear. Copy each product's design exactly: same shape, proportions, colors, materials and details. The product photos are studio catalog shots, often renders, giving the design only. Each product must look photographed by this camera in this room, lit by daylight from the balcony door, with matching white balance, contrast, grain, sharpness, contact shadows and real fabric creases and wood wear. Keep everything else unchanged: framing, walls, floor, light, AC. Add nothing else. Output a real photograph, not a render.

placements.where: left of balcony door, under switch
